entries.q: My boyfriend was accused of sexually assaulting a female in 2020. A week ago he was found guilty of the assault and he's waiting for his sentence. How can he get help, any help.?
entries.a: For someone convicted of sexual assault: - Seek counseling and rehabilitation - Comply with court-ordered penalties and restrictions - Consider seeking legal advice for appeal or post-conviction relief

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 355 of Chapter XVI-A in Pakistan Penal Code (Assault or criminal force with intent to dishonour person, otherwise than on grave provocation:).
entries.a: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any perso n, intending thereby to dishonour that person, otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 439 of Chapter XVII in Pakistan Penal Code (Punishment for intentionally running vessel aground or ashore with intent to commit theft, etc,:).
entries.a: Whoever intentionally runs any vessel aground or ashore, intending to commit theft of any property contained therein or to' dishonestly misappropriate any such property, or with intent that such theft or misappropriation of property may be committed, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

entries.q: Please explain Section 47 of Chapter III of Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (Relevancy of certain evidence for proving, in subsequent proceeding, the truth of facts therein stated).
entries.a: Evidence given by a witness in a judicial proceeding or before any person authorised by law to take it, is relevant for the; purpose of proving, in a subsequent judicial, proceeding or in a later stage of the same judicial proceeding, the truth of the facts which it states, when the witness is dead or cannot be found, or is incapable of giving evidence, or is kept out of the way by the adverse party, or if his presence cannot be obtained without an amount of delay or expense which, under the circumstances of the case, the Court considers unreasonable Provided that the proceeding was between the same parties or their representatives-in-interest; the adverse party in the first proceeding had the right and opportunity to cross-examine ; the questions in issue were substantially the same in the first as in the second proceeding. Explanation: A criminal trial or inquiry shall be deemed to be a proceeding between the prosecutor and the accused within the meaning of this Article. STATEMENTS MADE UNDER SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 72 of Chapter III in Pakistan Penal Code (Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, the judgment stating that it is doubtful of).
entries.a: which: In all cases in which judgment is given that a person is guilty of one of several offences specified in the judgment, but that it is doubtful of whic h of these offences he is guilty, the offender shall be punished for the offence for which the lowest punishment is provided if the same punishment is not provided, for all.

entries.q: Could you describe the contents of Section nan from Police Law (Safety and Police Complaints Commission shall be elected by the members from amongst themselves every three years)?
entries.a: Provided that the Chairperson of the District Public Safety Commission at the commencement of the Police Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004, shall continue to hold such office till completion of his term of office as Chairperson of the District Public Safety and Police Complaints Commission. (2) The Chairperson of the District Public Safety and Police Complaints Commission shall be eligible for re-election for the second term. (3) The Chairperson of the District Public Safety and Police Complaints Commission shall not be removed from his office save as provided for removal of a member of the Commission. (4) The Chairperson shall be entitled to honoraria and privileges as may be determined by the Government. ]

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 37 of Chapter III in Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (Confession caused by inducement, threat or promise, when irrelevant in criminal proceeding).
entries.a: A confession made by an accused person is irrelevant in a criminal proceeding, if the making of the confession appears to the Court to have been caused by any inducement, threat or promise having reference to the charge against the accused person, proceeding from a person in authority and sufficient, in the opinion of the Court, to give the accused person grounds which would appear to him reasonable, for supposing that by making it he would gain any advantage or avoid any evil of a temporal nature in reference to the proceedings against him.

entries.q: I pay my rent yearly. Does the landlord have the right to give me one week to move out just because I asked him to fix a leak in the house where water is gushing out from the sink?
entries.a: A landlord cannot simply ask a tenant paying yearly rent to vacate the property on short notice, especially if the tenant has requested necessary repairs. Tenant rights are protected by Nigerian law, specifically, the Tenancy Law of Lagos State (or similar tenancy laws in other states), which mandates proper notice periods and reasons for eviction. Key Points for a Tenant Paying Rent Yearly: Notice Requirement: According to most tenancy laws in Nigeria, a tenant paying rent annually is entitled to a minimum of six months' notice before eviction. A one-week notice is insufficient and does not comply with legal requirements. Right to Request Repairs: As a tenant, you have the right to ask the landlord to fix essential aspects of the property, such as plumbing or other facilities. It is the landlord’s responsibility to ensure the property remains habitable and meets minimum standards. Legal Grounds for Eviction: Unless there is a breach of lease terms (such as non-payment of rent), the landlord must follow due process for eviction, which includes giving proper notice and, if necessary, obtaining a court order. Seeking Legal Advice: If your landlord is pressuring you to leave on short notice, it’s advisable to consult with a legal professional to understand your rights and potentially obtain an injunction if harassment or illegal eviction attempts continue.

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 508 of Chapter XXII in Pakistan Penal Code (Act caused by inducing person to believe that he will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure:).
entries.a: Whoever voluntarily causes or attempts to cause any person to do anything which that person is not legally bound to do or to omit to do anything which he is legally entitled to do, by inducing or attempting to induce that person to believe that he or any p erson in whom he is interested will become or will be rendered by some act of the offender an object of Divine displeasure if he does not to the thing which it is the object of the offender to cause him to do, or if he does the thing which it is object of the offender to cause to him to omit shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Illustrations (a) A suits dhurna at Z's door with the intention of causing it to be b elieved that, by so sitting, he renders 2 an object of divine displeasure, A has committed the offence defined in this section. (b) A threatens Z that, unless Z performs a certain act, A wilt kill one of A's own children, under such circumstances that the killing would be believed to render Z an object of Divine displeasure. A has committed the offence defined in this section.

entries.q: Could you describe the contents of Section 27 from Transfer of Property Act (Conditional transfer to one person coupled with transfer to another on failure of prior disposition. )?
entries.a: Where, on a transfer of property, an interest therein is created in favour of one person, and by the same transaction an ulterior disposition of the same interest is made in favour of another, if the prior disposition under the transfer shall fail, the ulterior disposition shall take effect upon the failure of the prior disposition, although the failure may not have occurred in the manner contemplated by the transferor. But, where the intention of the parties to the transaction is that the ulterior disposition shall take effect, only in the event of the prior disposition failing in a particular manner, the ulterior disposition shall not take effect unless the prior disposition fails in that manner. Illustrations (a) A transfer Rs.500 to B on condition that he shall execute a certain lease within three months after A's death', and, if he should neglect to do so, to C. B dies in A's lifetime. The disposition in favour of C takes effect. (b) A transfer property to his wife, but, in case she should die in his lifetime, transfers to B that which he had transferred to her. A and his wife perish together, under circumstances which make it impossible to prove that she died before him. The disposition in favour of B does not take effect.

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 407 of Chapter XXXI in Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 ([Omitted by Item No. 140 of Punjab Notifi cation No. SO(J-II) 1-8/75 (P-V),dated 21-3-).
entries.a: 1996 for Punjab.]

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 458 of Chapter XVII in Pakistan Penal Code (Lurking house -trespass or house -breaking by night after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful).
entries.a: restraint: Whoever commits lurking house -trespass by night or house -breaking by night, having made preparation for causing hurt to any person, or for assaulti ng any person, or for wrongfully restraining any person, or for putting any person in fear of hurt, or of assault, or of wrongful restraint, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to fourteen years, and shall also be liable to fine. 167[

entries.q: What is stated in Section 25 of Chapter III of Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (In suits for damages facts tending to enable Court to determine amount are Facts not otherwise relevant)?
entries.a: In suits in which damages are claimed, any fact which will enable the Court to determine the amount of damages which ought to be awarded, is relevant.

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 429 of Chapter XVII in Pakistan Penal Code (Mischief by killing or maiming cattle, etc., of any value or any animal of the value of fifty rupees:).
entries.a: Whoever commits mischief by killing, poisoning, maiming or rendering useless, any elephant, camel, horse, mule, buffalo, bull, cow or ox, whatever may be the value thereof, or any other animal of the value of fifty rupees or upwards, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with both.

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 78 of Chapter V in Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document produced ).
entries.a: If a document is alleged to be signed or to have been written wholly or in part by any person, the signature or the handwriting of so much of the document as is alleged to be in that person's handwriting must be proved to be in his handwriting.

entries.q: Please explain Section 31 of Chapter II of Transfer of Property Act (Condition that transfer shall cease to have effect in case specified uncertain event happens or does not happen. ).
entries.a: Subject to the provisions of section 12, on a transfer of property an interest therein may be created with the condition superadded that it shall cease to exist in case a specified uncertain event shall happen, or in case a specified uncertain event shall not happen. Illustrations (a) A transfers a farm to B for his life, with a proviso that, in case B cuts down a certain wood, the transfer shall cease to have any effect. B cuts down the wood. He loses his life-interest in the farm. (b) A transfers a farm to B, provided that, if B shall not go to England within three years after the date of transfer, his interest in the farm shall cease. B does not go to England within the term prescribed. His interest in the farm ceases.

entries.q: I am planning to marry my Thai girlfriend soon. Her brother owns the land on which I wish to build a house. What are my rights and legal standing under Pakistani laws in this situation?
entries.a: As a foreigner marrying a Thai national in Pakistan: - Pakistani laws do not directly apply - Consider registering the marriage in Thailand or Pakistan

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 511 of Chapter XXIII in Pakistan Penal Code (Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or for a shorter terms).
entries.a: Whoever attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, or to cause such an offence to be committed, and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence, shall where no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such attempt, be punished with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one -half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for that offence or with such fine daman as is provided for the offence, or with both. Illustrations (a) A makes an attempt to steal some jewels by breaking, open the box, and finds after so opening the box, that there is no jewels in it. He has done an act towards the commission of theft , and therefore is guilty under this section. (b) A makes an attempt to pick the pocket of Z by thrusting his hand into Z's pocket, A fails in the attempt in consequence of 2's having nothing in his pocket. A is guilty under this section. Source:: (1) Punjab Police website. Pakistan Penal Code (as amended until 1997) in PDF - [http://www.punjabpolice.gov.pk/user_files/File/pakistan_penal_code_xlv_of_1860.pdf Source:: (2) Pakistan Penal Code (2004) - Nadeem Law Book House Source:: (3) Gazette of Pakistan Extraordinary, Jan 11, 2005 (Text of Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2004) Source:: (4) Text of Protection of Women (Criminal Laws

entries.q: Section 43 of Chapter III in Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (Consideration of proved confession affecting person making it and others jointly under trial for same offence): What does it say?
entries.a: When more persons than one are being tried jointly for the same offence and a confession made by one of such persons is proved,- (a) such confession shall be proof against the person , making it and; (b) the Court may take into consideration such confession as circumstantial evidence against such other person. Explanation: "Offence' as used in this Article, includes the abetment of or attempt to commit the offence.

entries.q: Give a brief explanation of Section 46 of Chapter III in Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (Cases in which statement of relevant fact by person who is dead or cannot be found, etc., is relevant).
entries.a: Statements, written or verbal, of relevant facts made by a person who is dead, or who cannot, be found, or, who has become incapable of giving evidence, or whose attendance can not be procured without an amount of delay or expense which under the circumstances of the case appears to the Court unreasonable, are themselves relevant facts in the following cases: (1) When it relates to cause of death: When the statement is made by a person as to the cause of his death, or as to any of the circumstances of the transaction which resulted in his death, in cases in which the cause of that person's death comes into question. Such statements are relevant whether the person who made them was or was not, at the time when they were made, under expectation of death, and whatever may be the nature of the proceeding in which cause of his death comes into question. (2) Or is made in course of business: When the statement is made by such person in the ordinary course of business, and in particular when it consists of any entry or memorandum made by him in books kept in the ordinary course of business.. or in the discharge of professional duty; or of an acknowledgment Written or signed by him of the receipt of money, goods, securities or property of any kind ; or of a document used in commerce written or signed by him ; or of the date of a letter or other document usually dated, written or signed

entries.q: Could you describe the contents of Section 107 from Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (Evidence as to application of language to one of two sets of facts to neither of which the whole correctly applies)?
entries.a: When the language used applies partly to one set of existing facts, and partly to another set of existing facts, but the whole of it does not apply correctly to either evidence may be given to show to which of the two it was meant to apply. Illustrations A agrees to sell to B "my land at X in the occupation of Y". A has land at X, but not in the occupation of Y, and he had land in the occupation of Y, but it is not at X. Evidence may be given of facts; which he meant to sell.

entries.q: What is stated in Section 127 of Chapter IX of Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (Proof of good faith in transactions where one party is in relation of active When the question is whether any person is)?
entries.a: When there is a question as to the good faith of a transaction between parties, one of whom stands to the other in a position of active confidence. The burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is on the party who is in a position of active confidence. Illustrations (a) The good faith of a sale by a client to an advocate is in question in a suit brought by the client. The burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is on the advocate. (b) The good faith of a sale by a son Just come of age to a father is in question in a suit brought by the son. The burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is on the father.

entries.q: Is there any legal justification for my landlord refusing to provide proof of depositing my security deposit into an interest-bearing account, as required under tenancy laws in Pakistan? Please clarify.
entries.a: Under Pakistani law, your landlord is required to provide proof of depositing your security deposit into an interest-bearing account. Failure to comply can result in legal action.

entries.q: I have three children, and their mother took them away to marry another man. She changed their names and converted them to Islam. What legal actions can I take to regain custody or address this situation?
entries.a: Your three Children were taken from you by their mum and yet you do not need a Lawyer. Well your option is you can forget about your kids and wait till they grow up without you in their lives hoping that someday, they remember you and come looking when they are all grown up. Then God help you if the foster father or anyone in their immediate environment molests them sexually. I hope they forgive you for not putting up a fight to get them back. I wish you the best in your quest.

entries.q: I currently have custody of my children after separating from their father. He is not a fraudster, and I hold a stable, legal job. How can I strengthen my case and fight to ensure my children remain with me?
entries.a: To strengthen your case for custody: - Document evidence (parenting plans, financial records) - Show proof of stability and suitability

entries.q: What is Section 40 of Chapter II of Transfer of Property Act (Burden of obligation imposing restriction on use of land, or of obligation annexed to ownership but not amounting to interest or easement.) about?
entries.a: Where, for the more beneficial enjoyment of his own immovable property, a third person has, independently of any interest in the immovable property, of another or of any easement thereon, a right to restrain the enjoyment 31[in a particular manner of the latter property], or Where third person is entitled to the benefit of an obligation arising out of contract, and annexed to the ownership of immovable property, but not amounting to an interest therein or easement thereon, such right or obligation may be enforced against a transferee with notice thereof or a gratuitous transferee of the property affected thereby, but not against a transferee for consideration and without notice of the right or obligation, nor against such property in his hands. Illustration. A contracts to sell 32[Ulipur] to B. While the contract is still in force, he sells [Ulipur] to C, who, has notice of the contract. B may enforce the contract against C to the same extent as against A.

entries.q: What is stated in Section 53 of Chapter III of Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (What evidence to be given when statement forms part of a conversation, When the Court document, book or series of letters or papers)?
entries.a: When any statement of which evidence is given forms part of a longer statement, or of a conversation or part of an isolated document, or is contained in a document which forms part of a book or of a connected series of letters or papers, evidence shall be given of so much and no more of the statement, conversation, document, book or series of letters or papers as the Court considers necessary in that particular case to the full understanding of the nature and effect of the statement, and of the circumstances under which it was made. JUDGMENTS OF COURTS OF JUSTICE WHEN RELEVANT

entries.q: I received threats of termination from my superior, which forced me to resign unwillingly to avoid having a termination record in my career. Do I have the right to sue or seek legal protection in this situation?
entries.a: To address threats of termination: - Document incidents and communications - File with HR or labor department

entries.q: My wife, a Pakistani citizen, ran away to Qatar and took my son, who is also a Pakistani citizen, with her. I want to file a police complaint against my wife and seek her deportation along with my son. Both are Pakistani citizens
entries.a: To file a complaint against your wife: - Gather evidence (custody agreements, witness statements) - File with Pakistani authorities (Federal Investigation Agency)

entries.q: My brother moved to Canada in 2023, and for his immigration paperwork, we declared him as unemployed until 2023. He did not pay income tax in Pakistan nor was he registered for it. How can I obtain a certificate of non-income tax for him?
entries.a: To get a non-income tax certificate, apply to the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) with required documents.

entries.q: What legal remedies are available in Pakistan if a brother refuses to share their father's property with a sister, solely on the basis of her gender? What steps can the sister take to claim her rightful inheritance under Pakistani inheritance laws?
entries.a: If your brother won't share property, you can file a partition suit in civil court. Gather proof of your inheritance rights and be prepared for a potentially lengthy process.

entries.q: I have been separated for more than 16 years now. I only have 1 daughter who is now 29 years old. I would like to request an assessment, what are the necessary documents needed? How long would it take to get an annulment and how much would it cost.
entries.a: Necessary documents for annulment assessment: - Marriage certificate - Proof of separation - Identification documents - Grounds for annulment

entries.q: Can I legally pursue action against a girl for making false accusations? She falsely claimed that I said something to her which I did not, thereby tarnishing my reputation. What are my legal rights and options in such a situation under Pakistani law?
entries.a: Pursuing action for false accusations: - File a complaint with the police or court - Provide evidence of false accusations - Seek damages or compensation for reputational harm

entries.q: I am writing to inquire about the specific regulatory and licensing requirements for operating cryptocurrency ATMs in Pakistan. Could you please provide detailed information on the type of license or authorization that operators need to obtain under Pakistani law?
entries.a: In Pakistan, the regulatory and licensing requirements for operating cryptocurrency ATMs are governed by the State Bank of Pakistan and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan. Operators need to obtain the necessary licenses and authorizations.

entries.q: My ex-partner is refusing to sell assets or finalize the divorce, which is preventing me from achieving a fair financial order. What legal options do I have under Pakistani law to address this situation and ensure a fair division of assets during the divorce process?
entries.a: Addressing refusal to sell assets or finalize divorce: - File a lawsuit for division of assets - Seek court intervention to finalize divorce - Negotiate a settlement with your partner

entries.q: I have given loan to a family and now they are not paying it back even after 3 years of wait. I need to send them a legal notice to settle the case in court if they will not pay it back. Is ot possible to first use legal notice as a way to compel them to pay my koan back.?
entries.a: Yes, it is absolutely possible to send a legal notice to the family demanding repayment of the loan. If you wish, I can assist you in drafting and sending the legal notice to ensure it effectively communicates the seriousness of the matter. Alongside availing civil remedy for recovery, you can also initiate criminal proceeding under relevant provisions. For more query, kindly do consult our legal team at below given contact details.

entries.q: Can I file a case against the driver responsible for my sister’s death, even though the company he works for has covered all hospital and burial expenses? What legal actions can I take under Pakistani law to seek justice for my sister? Thank you, and I look forward to your guidance.
entries.a: You can file a case against the driver responsible for your sister's death, specifically under Section 304 of the Pakistan Penal Code, which deals with culpable homicide. You can seek compensation and justice under Pakistani law, including damages for pain and suffering, medical expenses, and loss of income. (Relevant law: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860)

entries.q: I was copied in an email accusing me of promising a tender for supplying a motorbike to my workplace and then short-changing the client. This email was sent to my employer and colleagues. I have not been involved in any tender process, but my job is now at risk. What steps can I take?
entries.a: To address false accusations: - Gather evidence (emails, witness statements) - File with HR or police

entries.q: I have been separated from my husband for 9 years because of his bad treatment and interference from his family. He has never cared to see our two children but now wants joint custody or wants them to visit him on weekends. The children are 8 and 10 years old. As their mother, what should I do?
entries.a: Having been separated for a period of more than 3 years, the court will certainly dissolve your marriage.

entries.q: My 17-year-old brother has been detained without a search warrant or an arrest warrant and is being asked to provide bail in the amount of Rs. 29,000. Could you please guide me on the legality of this detention under Pakistani law and the appropriate steps we can take to address this situation?
entries.a: The detention of your brother is illegal under Pakistani law, specifically Article 10 of the Constitution of Pakistan, which guarantees the right to a fair trial. You can file a habeas corpus petition in the high court to challenge the detention. The court will examine the circumstances of the detention and determine whether it is lawful. (Relevant law: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898)

entries.q: The land my wife and I purchased, where we built a house, was originally platted based on a provincial road. The provincial road was later straightened, and our property is no longer directly accessible from the new road. Do we have a legal claim to a right of way along the original road alignment?
entries.a: To claim a right of way: - Review original property deeds and maps - Document the original road alignment - Negotiate with the provincial government or adjacent landowners

entries.q: My husband and I are foreigners living in Thailand for six years. We signed a contract outlining our mutual obligations, but it lacks a lawyer's signature and seal. Is it legally binding? What are the costs of formalizing such a contract, and will it hold legal weight in court if a clause is breached?
entries.a: To formalize a contract in Thailand: - Register with the Thai Ministry of Commerce - Notarize the contract for added authenticity

entries.q: I want to leave my marriage due to my husband’s abuse, including physical violence and threats. He also threatens to take my children away from me after sending me out of the house because I caught him cheating. What legal steps can I take in Pakistan to protect myself and secure custody of my children?
entries.a: To protect yourself and secure custody in Pakistan: - File a complaint with the local police or a protection committee - Obtain a protection order under the Protection of Women Against Violence Act - File for custody under the Guardians and Wards Act

entries.q: For certain reasons, the title documents of the house I built in Nigeria are in my wife’s name (her marital name). She left me while I was in the United States, and now I have returned to Pakistan to stay in the house. Can I claim legal ownership of the house under Pakistani law, given these circumstances?
entries.a: You may be able to claim legal ownership of the house under Pakistani law, specifically the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. However, the court will consider the circumstances and the intention of the parties, including whether the property was purchased with your money or whether you have contributed to the mortgage payments. (Relevant law: Transfer of Property Act, 1882)

entries.q: My ex-husband divorced me under Sharia law, but I am not a Muslim. How can I legally nullify my marriage? Our marriage certificate already shows the divorce, but since I am not a Muslim, the embassy in Hong Kong refuses to register my new marriage, saying the Sharia divorce does not apply to me. What should I do?
entries.a: get decree from the local court by filing declaratory suit that the divorce given is the valid one.

entries.q: I want to return the bride price and also seek child support, as I have been taking care of the children single-handedly for the past four years. How can I go about this under Pakistani law, and what would be the expected legal costs involved in filing for the return of the bride price and claiming child support?
entries.a: To return the bride price and seek child support, you'll need to file a petition in family court. Be prepared to provide proof of single-handedly caring for the children.

entries.q: My friend has been in the process of having her foreign divorce recognized in Cebu for over three years. The presiding judge keeps requesting additional documentation that seems unnecessary according to the law. What actions can she take to expedite the process, update her NBI status, and proceed with remarrying?
entries.a: To expedite foreign divorce recognition in Cebu: - File a motion to expedite - Cite undue delay - Provide required documents (divorce decree, marriage certificate)

entries.q: I need an experienced lawyer to support a divorce initiated by a woman. The couple is of Indian origin, and they are unable to reach an agreement for divorce. The woman seeks to file for divorce under Pakistani law. What are the legal steps involved, and how can a lawyer assist in ensuring the process is completed effectively?
entries.a: For divorce initiated by a woman under Pakistani law: - File a petition with the family court - Provide grounds for divorce (e.g., cruelty, desertion) - Negotiate a settlement or contest the divorce

entries.q: A buyer purchased a house and lot, paying in full, but the former owner failed to release the title before passing away. It has now been almost 40 years, and the children or survivors of the buyer have been living in the house. What legal steps can be taken now to secure the title of the property, considering the extended period of time?
entries.a: In cases of adverse possession, the key is to prove continuous possession, use, and occupation of the property. File a petition under Section 27-30 of the Limitation Act, 1908, and provide strong evidence to support your claim.

entries.q: My girlfriend is refusing to allow my child to visit and stay with me, even though she is not around and has left the child with her parents while she is away for a one-year service. I am available and willing to care for my child. What legal steps can I take under Pakistani law to establish visitation rights or custody in this situation?
entries.a: To get visitation rights or custody, file a petition in family court. Show proof that you're available and willing to care for the child.

entries.q: In cases of divorce, if the husband has sold out all the properties belonging to him before finalizing the divorce, is there any legal provision in Pakistani law that entitles the wife to a share of these properties? Similar to laws in other countries where the wife may be entitled to 50% of the properties as of the last date they stayed together?
entries.a: Wife's share of properties sold before divorce: - Pakistani law does not automatically entitle the wife to 50% of properties - Court may consider factors like income, expenses, and financial needs

entries.q: My parents passed away, and their property hasn’t been fully divided. I inherited the main house, while the rest of the land was divided among my siblings. Now my siblings are arguing about their shares. What are my rights in this situation? I am the only one maintaining the property, living in the house, and taking care of it. No one else lives here.
entries.a: The Pakistan Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937, and the Inheritance Act, 1925, govern inherited property in Pakistan. To protect your rights, gather relevant documents, including the property deed, inheritance certificate, proof of heirship, and proof of maintenance and care of the property. Reviewing the relevant laws and seeking assistance from a lawyer specializing in inheritance law may also be necessary.

entries.q: I am a mother of a 4-month-old baby currently living in Doha. I want to file for divorce from my husband due to his physical abuse, which I can prove with evidence and a police report. Could you please guide me on the steps to initiate divorce proceedings under Pakistani law, my rights regarding custody of my baby, and an estimate of the legal costs involved?
entries.a: You can file for divorce under Pakistani law, specifically the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961, which allows for divorce on the grounds of physical abuse. You will need to provide evidence, including the police report, medical records, and witness statements. You have the right to seek custody of your child, and the court will consider the child's best interests when making a decision. (Relevant law: Family Courts Act, 1964)

entries.q: My wife and I want to change my stepdaughter's last name. My wife, who is Thai, has taken my last name after marriage, and we would like my stepdaughter to have the same last name as us. My wife has sole custody of the child, and my stepdaughter is 5 years old. What is the legal process in Pakistan for changing the child’s last name under these circumstances?
entries.a: To change your stepdaughter's last name, file a petition in family court. Provide proof of sole custody and consent from the child's father (if applicable).

entries.q: The defendant has fled illegally to Sri Lanka and is working there. Despite having assets and bank accounts, the court order and flight ban in the UAE are no longer effective. We now need to pursue the case in Sri Lankan courts. What legal options do we have to enforce the court’s decision in Sri Lanka, and can we compel the defendant to pay the required amount?
entries.a: To enforce a court decision in Sri Lanka: - File an application with the Sri Lankan courts - Provide proof of the UAE court decision - Seek assistance from the Sri Lankan authorities

entries.q: We are married, and my husband has another woman (mistress) with whom he has fathered a child. He claims that his only obligation is to provide for the child he has with the mistress, and that he has no further obligation towards me. How does this situation affect my rights and what legal recourse do I have, especially considering my difficulty in finding employment?
entries.a: Your rights as a wife in Pakistan: - Maintenance and financial support - Custody of children - Protection from harassment File a petition with the family court to enforce your rights.

entries.q: I moved into a rental just over a month ago, and since then, there have been nothing but problems with the landlords. The place was infested with rats the day I moved in, and I had to take care of that myself, along with other issues that they won’t fix. Two days ago, they gave me a 30-day notice to move out with a vague excuse. Do you handle these types of situations?
entries.a: When dealing with a rental dispute, documentation is critical. Contest the 30-day notice under Section 14 of the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 (or the relevant provincial law), and provide evidence of all issues with the landlord.

entries.q: I am a salesman, and our distributor's warehouse was burgled, with goods worth 37 million being stolen. I, along with other staff, was arrested and detained because the distributor suspected us. Before the arrest, I had collected goods worth 350,000 which I have not yet paid for. Should I pay the money owed first, or should I seek legal advice and take legal action regarding the situation?
entries.a: In such cases, it's crucial to act quickly. File a case under Section 491 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) to seek compensation for the wrongful detention. Ensure you gather all evidence, including witness statements, to build a strong case.

entries.q: I have been admitted to a Master's program at Nova SBE in Portugal. However, I have a history of visa rejections from the USA (tourist and student), Canada (tourist and student), and Sweden (study permit). What steps can I take to strengthen my case for a Portuguese student visa, given my prior rejections? Would hiring a lawyer to review my application and provide guidance improve my chances?
entries.a: To strengthen your case for a Portuguese student visa: - Provide a clear explanation for prior rejections - Show proof of admission to Nova SBE - Demonstrate sufficient funds and language proficiency - Consider submitting additional documentation, such as a letter of recommendation

entries.q: We are the parents of a newborn son and have been waiting for an interview call for 10 months. We have two minor children under the age of 12. Our I-130 petitions were approved and filed separately under the F-41 visa category. Both children are mentioned and included in the main application submitted to USCIS. Since they are minors, how can we accompany them to the United States? Please advise.
entries.a: To accompany your minor children to the United States, you will need to provide documentation, including proof of your relationship and the children's birth certificates. You may also need to obtain a visa for the children.

entries.q: My mother was the sole survivor among her large family. The issue is that one of my aunts transferred land to her name, and the other aunt built a house on land that belonged to her sibling. Both aunts are now deceased. However, my aunt's son-in-law is claiming ownership of the land and the house. What legal actions can be taken to resolve this dispute, and how can my mother protect her rights to the property?
entries.a: To resolve the property dispute, your mother should file a suit for declaration and possession under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. It's essential to gather all relevant documents, including the original deed, inheritance documents, and any other proof of ownership.

entries.q: The mother of my child has left the child with her parents. The mother and I are not married, and she has no intention of adding my name to the child’s birth certificate. Additionally, the grandparents' residence does not have its own electricity and relies on illegal electricity tapping from neighbors. Under Pakistani law, is it possible for me to obtain full or partial custody of the child, given these circumstances?
entries.a: Under Pakistani law, you may be able to obtain full or partial custody of the child. The court will consider the child's best interests and the parents' circumstances.

entries.q: My son, who is 33 years old and holds a U.S. green card valid until 2032, has overstayed in the Philippines for more than a year due to mental illness, making it difficult for him to travel alone. Can he return to the United States despite his overstay, and what legal or procedural steps can I take to assist him? Additionally, are there any requirements under Pakistani law that I must fulfill to facilitate his travel and care?
entries.a: To assist your son in returning to the US: - Gather documentation (green card, passport, medical records) - File a request for humanitarian parole or reinstatement

entries.q: I am looking for a lawyer experienced in handling Portuguese student visa applications, particularly for individuals with prior visa rejections. My case involves acceptance to Nova SBE and previous denials from the USA, Canada, and Sweden. What specific concerns should be addressed in my application to mitigate the impact of my prior rejections? Do you specialize in Portuguese student visas and have experience with similar cases?
entries.a: To address prior rejections in a Portuguese student visa application: - Explain the reasons for prior rejections - Highlight any changes in circumstances - Emphasize your commitment to studying in Portugal

entries.q: I had a traditional marriage with my wife on March 6, 2021, and we signed an agreement on March 5, 2021, stating, "There shall be no divorce." Recently, without seeking a customary or legal divorce, my wife secretly entered into a court marriage with another man. This occurred two weeks ago, and I wish to nullify her court marriage, as it breaches our agreement and the laws of Pakistan. What legal steps can I take to address this situation?
entries.a: To nullify the court marriage: - File a petition with the family court - Provide evidence of the prior marriage and agreement - Argue that the second marriage is invalid under Pakistani law

entries.q: How can I initiate a legal case in Pakistan against a person from Gujrat and their family who committed money fraud? I have proof of my claims. Even though I am not in Pakistan, can a lawyer help me recover my financial losses and pursue legal action to hold them accountable? Additionally, they have committed other crimes, for which I also have evidence. My primary concern is recovering my money, but I want to ensure all crimes are addressed.
entries.a: To initiate a legal case in Pakistan: - Gather evidence (contracts, emails, financial records) - File with Pakistani authorities (Federal Investigation Agency)

entries.q: I hope this message finds you well. I am seeking assistance regarding the reinstatement of my immigration case with the National Visa Center (NVC). My case was filed under the F1 category in 2005, but I was unable to proceed after 2017 due to personal circumstances, including my family responsibilities. Could you guide me on how to reinstate my case and what steps are required under Pakistani legal and procedural guidelines for immigration matters?
entries.a: To reinstate your immigration case with the National Visa Center (NVC), you will need to provide documentation, including proof of your relationship and the reasons for the delay. You will also need to complete a new visa application and pay the required fees.

entries.q: We are not separated yet, but my husband is planning to initiate separation. I want to know if I can secure custody of my three children, aged 11, 8, and 1. The children mean everything to me. We had a traditional and church wedding but not a court wedding. My husband is a businessman, and I am a civil servant employed by the government. Is it possible for me to retain custody of the children? Also, during our 10-year marriage, he has physically abused me twice on separate occasions.
entries.a: To secure custody of your children: - Document evidence (witness statements, medical records) - File with the family court

entries.q: I am 25 years old and planning to create a fictional work as a franchise, potentially including artwork and video games. I want to ensure my ideas and creations are protected before sharing them with freelancers to avoid theft or leaks. How can I file for copyright in Pakistan? Does Pakistani copyright law protect my work internationally? Who should I contact for legal advice on this matter, and what are the requirements and costs associated with registering and owning a franchise or brand?
entries.a: To file for copyright in Pakistan, submit an application to the Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan (IPO-Pakistan) with: - A copy of the work - Proof of ownership - Payment of the required fee Pakistani copyright law protects works internationally under the Berne Convention.

entries.q: I have been separated from my husband for over 15 years. I was a battered wife, as he would often physically hurt me, especially when drunk, which led me to leave him. After the separation, I took custody of our four children, and he has not provided any financial support since then. The only assistance I receive is 4,000 PKR per month from his mother. If I file for a nullity of marriage, is it likely to be approved under Pakistani law? Additionally, how much would the legal process cost me?
entries.a: Nullity of marriage may be approved if: - The marriage was not consummated - There was lack of consent - The marriage was not registered Costs vary depending on the complexity of the case and lawyer fees.

entries.q: I purchased a 65' Power Catamaran from a boat builder in Rayong with an agreed completion time of 10 months. Construction started on March 1, 2021, but the boat remains unfinished after 2.5 years. The total cost was $1,400,000, paid in 8 installments of $175,000. I made 7 payments within the first year based on the builder's assurance that 7 stages were complete, which was not accurate. Despite repeated promises of completion within 2 months, the project remains unfinished. Can I reclaim my payments with interest?
entries.a: To reclaim payments for the unfinished boat: - Review the contract and documentation - File with the consumer protection agency

entries.q: My wife constantly insults and abuses me during misunderstandings, leading to hatred and bitterness between us. Strong words have been exchanged, and both of us find it difficult to reconcile even with the intervention of a third party. The marriage has become toxic for both of us, and we are both now in agreement that we want to end the marriage. We have a son who is less than a year old. What are my legal options under Pakistani law for ending this marriage and addressing custody and financial matters for our child?
entries.a: Ending a toxic marriage and addressing custody: - File for divorce on grounds of cruelty or irreconcilable differences - Seek custody of the child based

entries.q: My business partner falsely accused me of stealing money from the safe, banned me from the business, and unilaterally decided that I am a silent partner without my consent. Despite my repeated requests, he has refused to apologise for the unproven and distressing allegations. I am now looking to sell my shares in the company back to him. I initially invested 800,000 PKR but he is only offering 350,000 PKR. I have another buyer interested, but he is not proceeding with the purchase. What legal options do I have to recover my investments or protect my rights under Pakistani law?
entries.a: Recovering investments in a business partnership: - File a lawsuit for breach of contract - Seek arbitration or mediation - Negotiate a settlement with your partner

entries.q: I have two children born out of wedlock who currently reside in the Philippines. Since their birth, I have not had custody of them, and their surnames follow their father. The children have not wanted me in their lives either. Now, they wish to study abroad, which under the law requires my consent to undertake responsibility.I have been living and working overseas for many years and do not wish to take responsibility for them anymore, as I feel this situation is unfair to me. I would like to know the legal process under Pakistani law to formally sever ties and absolve myself of any legal responsibility for the children.
entries.a: To sever ties with your children, file a petition in family court. Provide proof of abandonment and lack of involvement.

entries.q: I require advice regarding a long-term visa for Italy. I am an Israeli citizen, 75 years old, retired, with a capital of approximately five million dollars. I am interested in purchasing residential property in the lake area in northern Italy and am inquiring about obtaining a long-term visa. I do not work and have no need for employment or business in Italy. My wife and I are a couple without children. My average annual income from investments and trading in the capital market exceeds 100 thousand euros. If necessary, I can provide documentation in the prescribed format. I am currently near Verona and would like to schedule a meeting with a lawyer for further advice.
entries.a: For a long-term visa in Italy, provide: - Proof of income (€100,000+) - Property purchase or rental in Italy - Health insurance - Valid passport

entries.q: I worked part-time with a company for 1 year and 8 months but quit a week ago due to being in another country longer than expected because of flight cancellations. I informed my manager via message, saying, "I will not be working with this company anymore, thank you."During my employment, I felt undervalued, overworked, and poorly compensated, which led to my decision to leave. If I reapply and work for the company again but later decide to quit after a short period, can I seek compensation for the work I did, given the lack of respect and value I experienced? Is there a way to file a claim or write a formal statement outlining these reasons to seek financial redress for my service and treatment during my employment?
entries.a: You can't get compensation for past work, but you can file a labor court complaint for unfair treatment.

entries.q: The landlord at my former residence agreed to return a portion of my Rs. 11,000 security deposit, retaining Rs. 8,000 for cleaning. While she provided a quotation for Rs. 2,000, no other receipts or proof of expenses have been shared to justify the deductions. I believe the cleaning was unnecessary, as I have photographic evidence of the condition in which I left the property. Additionally, the landlord has not responded to my request for proof that the security deposit was placed in an interest-bearing account. There are no outstanding dues, and all repairs have reportedly been made. Should I proceed through the rent controller under the tenancy laws, or are there alternative legal remedies available to resolve this dispute?
entries.a: You can proceed through the rent controller under the tenancy laws. The Rent Controller can help resolve the dispute and ensure the landlord refunds the security deposit.

entries.q: I am planning to work abroad but am concerned about leaving my three children (ages 20, 18, and 10) with their father, who is an alcoholic and verbally abusive when drunk. I fear for their safety and well-being as he has a history of prioritizing drinking over his responsibilities and often creates a toxic environment at home. Can I establish a legal agreement in Pakistan to limit his access to the children, particularly my 10-year-old daughter, to supervised visits on specific days, ensuring he is not under the influence of alcohol? If he violates this agreement, can restrictions be placed, such as maintaining a set distance from the children at home or school? Should I approach the Family Court, Social Welfare Department, or seek legal advice to ensure my children’s safety?
entries.a: To establish supervised visits: - Document evidence (police reports, medical records) - File with the family court.

fullTexts.title: ACCEDING STATE (PROPERTY) ORDER, 1961
fullTexts.t:
THE ACCEDING STATE (PROPERTY) ORDER, 1961 
 
PRESIDENT ’S ORDER NO. 12 OF 196l  
[22 August, 1961]  
 
In pursuance of the Proclamation of the seventh day of October,1958, and in exercise of all 
powers enabling him in that behalf, the President is  pleased to make the following Order: — 
 
1.— (1) This Order may be called the Acceding State  (Property) Order, 1 961. 
 
(2) It shall come into force at once, but an order  made in pursuance of it may be  given 
retrospective effect to a date not earlier than the fifteenth day of August 1947.  
 
2. In this Order, references to a State shall be construed as references to a S tate which has at 
any time after the 14th day  of August 1947 been in accession with Pakistan, and references  to a Ruler 
shall be construed as including references to the Ruler  of such a State and to the person recognized for 
the time being under the Rulers  (Recognition of Successors) Order, 1960, as  successor of the Ruler . 
 
3. Where any question arises directly or indirectly between persons claiming to be the heirs 
and successors of the Ruler of a state or claiming to succeed to the State, concerning the  devolution 
and distribution of any property of that State or of th e Ruler, the question shall be decided by an order 
of the  1[Federal Government].  
 
4. A question whether any disposition of property, whether purporting to be the property of the 
State or of th e Ruler, has been made in the due exercise of power to make it or ought for any reason to 
be undone shall be deemed to be a question falling under the preceding Article.  
 
5.—(1) Where the decision requires the recovery of a sum of money the order shall direct that 
the sum be recovered as an arrear of land revenue, and where it requires the recovery of any other 
property it shall direct the attachment of such property by seizur e, and upon the sum being recovered 
or the property being attached, the same shall forthwith be at the disposal of the  1[Federal Government] 
and shall be disposed of by the  1[Federal Government] by direction in such a way as may best give 
effect to the decision.  
 
(2) An order requiring recovery shall be directed to the Deputy Commissioner, and an order 
requiring attachment shall be directed to the District Magistrate, of the district concerned and he shall 
cause it to be executed according to its tenor.  
 
(3) Where the property is other than money, and has been lost   or  destroy ed or otherwise 
dispose d of and is irrecoverable the 1[Federal Government] may assess its value in money and order  
the recovery of an equivalent sum as an arrear of land revenue as provided in clause (1 ). 
 
6. All expenses incurred by the 1[Federal  Government] in  determining any question referred to 
it under Article 3 and all expenses incidental or consequential thereto shall be recoverable from the 
property to which the dispute relat es, and shall be the first charge thereon.  
 
  
7. No Court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any such question as is referred to in Article 3, 
and no Court shall call in  question any order of the 1[Federal  Government] made under that Article or 
Article 5 or any proceedings connected therewith.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1Subs. by Ord. III of 2000 , s.2, for “ Provincial  Government”, which previously subs. by F.A.O., 1975, Art. 2 & Sch. for “Central Government”.

THE APPRENTICESHIP ORDINANCE, 1962
1ORDINANCE No. LVI OF 1962
 [6th June, 1962]
 An Ordinance to make provision for promoting, developing and regulating systematic
apprenticeship programmes in the in dustries and for securing certain minimum standards of
skill.
WHEREAS it is expedient to make provision for promoting, developing and regulating systematic
apprenticeship programmes in the industries and for securing certain minimum standards of skill;
NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of the Proclamation of the seventh day of October, 1958, and
in exercise of all powers enabl ing him in that behalf, the President is pleased to make and promulgate
the following Ordinance:­
1. Short title, extent and commencement.­(1) This Ordinance may be called the Apprenticeship
Ordinance, 1962.
(2)        It extends to the whole of Pakistan.
(3)        It shall come into force on such date or dates and in respect of such undertakings as the
 2[Provincial Government] may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint in this behalf.
2. Definitions. In this Ordinance, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,­
(a) “apprentice” means a person undergoing training through the system of apprenticeship;
(b) “apprenticeable trade” means such trade or occupation as the competent authority may,
from time to time, keeping in view­
1This Ordinance has been applied to the Provincially Administered Tribal Area or to the parts of those areas to which it does not already apply, see¸ Regulation No. I of 1972, s. 2
and Sch. 
2Subs. by A.O., 1964, Art. 2 and Sch., for “Central Government”.
Page 2 of 8(i) the nature of the trade and the degree of skill involved therein; and
(ii) the amount of practical training and related theo retical instruction necessary for
attaining the laid down standards of skill and proficiency in the trade, declare, by
notification in the official Gazette, to be an apprenticeable trade for the purposes
of this Ordinance;
(c) “apprenticeship” means a system of training in which an employer undertakes to employ a
person and to train him or have him trained systematically in an apprenticeable trade for a
period the duration of which has been fixed in advance and in the course of which the
apprentice is bound to work in the employer’s service;
1[(d) “competent authority” means such officer as the Provincial Government may, by
notification in the official Gazette, appoint to be a competent authority for the purposes
of this Ordinance;]
 (e) “employer” means any person who employs five or more persons in an apprenticeable
trade in an under  taking, either directly or through another person, whether on behalf of
himself or any other person, and includes any person who has ultimate control over, or is
responsible to the owner thereof for, the affairs of an undertaking;
(f) “industrial establishment” shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in the 2[West
Pakistan Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968
(W.P. Ord. No. VI of 1968)];   
(g) “prescribed” means prescribed by rules;
(h) “rules” means rules made under this Ordinance;
(i) “undertaking” means any industrial establishment wherein fifty or more persons are
employed, or were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months.
3. Tripartite Advisory Committees. The  3[Provincial Government] may, by notification in the
official Gazette, constitute in the prescribed manner such  4[Provincial and Regional Tripartite
Advisory Committees] to advise the  3[Provincial Government] and the competent autho rity on
matters relating to apprenticeship as it may consider necessary.
 
1Subs. by A.O., 1964, Art. 2 and Sch., for original cl. (d) 
2Subs. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (27 of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II, for certain words. 
3Subs. by A.O., 1964, Art. 2 and Sch., for “Central Government”. 
4Subs. ibid., for “National and Regional Tripartite Advisory Committees”.
Page 3 of 84. Obligations of employers. Subject to the other provisions of this Ordinance and the rules, an
employer ­
(1) shall be bound to ensure proper compliance with the provisions of this Ordinance and the
rules in his under taking;
(2) shall, in accordance with the rules, introduce and operate an apprenticeship programme in
his under taking and get the programme registered with the competent authority within
such time as may be pres cribed;
(3) shall train apprentices in the proportion of a minimum of twenty per cent of the total
number of persons employed in apprenticeable trades, on an average in his undertaking,
or in such other proportion as the competent authority may, by order in writing, deter mine
in respect of his undertaking;
(4) who had already introduced an apprenticeship pro gramme in his undertaking prior to the
commence ment of this Ordinance shall modify the programme so as to bring it in
conformity with the provisions of this Ordinance and the rules and register such modified
programme with the competent authority within such time as may be prescribed;
(5) shall be responsible to ensure that an apprentice re ceives within the normal working hours
related theore tical instruction to the extent of at least twenty percent of the total working
hours;
(6) shall initiate and operate an apprenticeship programme entirely at his own cost; and
(7) shall not, without the approval in writing of the com petent authority, engage as an
apprentice any person who has been an apprentice with another employer and has left his
apprenticeship or been discharged by such other employer on disciplinary grounds.
5. Relief from income­tax etc.­(1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary con tained in the
 1[Income Tax Ordinance,1979 (XXXI of 1979)] income­tax shall not be pay able by an employer in
respect of any expenditure incurred by him on the operation of an apprenticeship programme in
accor dance with the provisions of this Ordinance and the rules.
(2) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the Imports and Exports (Control) Act,
1950 (XXXIX of 1950), or any rule or order made thereunder, the  2[Federal Government] may, by
order, make provision for the grant to the employers of licences for the import of such goods or
articles as may in its opinion be required by the employers for operating apprenticeship pro grammes
under this Ordinance.
1 Subs. by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (27 of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II, for certain words. 
2 Subs. by F.A.O., 1975,Art. 2 and Table, for “Central Government”.
Page 4 of 86. Advice and guidance to employers.­(1) Subject to the provisions of this Ordinance and the
rules, the competent authority shall offer to the employers all possible technical advice and guidance
in all matters relating to the apprenticeship programmes put into operation by the em ployers in their
undertakings in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance and the rules.
7. Obligations of apprentices.­(1) Subject to the other provisions of this Ordinance and the rules,
an apprentice­
(a) shall learn his trade conscientiously and diligently and shall endeavour to qualify himself
as a skilled worker on the completion of his apprenticeship;
(b) shall attend the practical training and related theoretical instruction according to the
programme laid down by the employer;
(c) shall carry out all lawful orders of the employer or his representative relating to his
apprenticeship and shall fulfil his obligations under the contract of apprentice ship;
(d) shall submit himself to any test or examination held from time to time for assessing the
progress of his training;
(e) shall not become the member of a Trade Union of any class of employees other than his
own;
(f) shall, in case of any grievance against his employer arising out or his apprenticeship,
approach the com petent authority for the redress of the grievance, if the same is not
redressed by the employer, and shall abide by the decision of the competent authority;
and
(g) shall not, without the previous approval in writing of the competent authority, leave his
apprenticeship after the completion of his probationary period.
(2) If an apprentice fails to carry out the terms of the contract of apprenticeship, or if at any time
during the period of his appren ticeship voluntarily quits such apprenticeship, or there are conti nued
adverse reports regarding the progress of his studies, or he is discharged for misconduct which shall
include insubordi nation, breach of the rules, absence from duty or neglect of his work, then he or, as
the case may be, his parent or guardian and the surety shall jointly and severally be liable to the
payment of such refund of expenses and compensation as may be prescribed.
8. Powers of entry, inspection, etc.­(1) Subject to any rules made in this behalf, the compe tent
authority may­
(a) with such assistants, if any, as it thinks fit, enter, inspect and examine any undertaking or
part thereof at any reasonable time;
(b) examine any apprentice employed therein or require the production of any register, record
or other docu ments maintained in pursuance of this Ordinance
Page 5 of 8and take on the spot or otherwise statements of any person which it may consider
necessary for carrying out the purposes of this Ordinance;
(c) make such examination and inquiry as it thinks fit in order to ascertain whether the
provisions of this Ordi nance and the rules are being observed in the under taking;
(d) exercise such other powers as may be prescribed.
(2) Notwithstanding anything in sub­section (1), no person shall be compelled under this section
to answer any question or make any statement which may tend directly or indirectly to incriminate
him.
9. Delegation of powers. Subject to any rules made in this behalf, the competent authority may,
by order in writing, direct that any power confer red upon it by or under this Ordinance, shall be
exercisable, also by such officer subordinate to it and subject to such conditions, if any, as may be
specified in the order.
10. Offences, penalties and procedure.­(1) If any employer­
(a) fails to engage the number of apprentices he is required to engage under section 4; or
(b) fails to carry out the terms and conditions of a con tract of apprenticeship; or
(c) refuses or neglects to furnish any information required to be furnished by him; or
(d) furnishes or causes to be furnished any information which is false and which he either
knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true; or
(e) refuses or neglects to afford the competent authority or an officer authorised by it any
reasonable facility for making an entry, inspection, examination or in quiry authorized by
or under this Ordinance; or
(f) engages an apprentice otherwise than in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance
and the rules; or
(g) otherwise contravenes any provision of this Ordinance or the rules;
he shall be punishable with a fine which may extend to ten thou sand rupees or, in default of payment
thereof, with imprisonment which may extend to six months, and in the case of a continuing offence
with a further fine which may extend to two hundred rupees for every day after the first during which
the offence con tinues:
            Provided that an offence repeated ninety days or more after the award of the previous
punishment shall not be deemed to be a continuing offence for the purpose of this section.
            (2) No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Ordinance save on
complaint made by the competent authority.
Page 6 of 8(3) No court inferior to that of a Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable
under this Ordinance.
11. Power to exempt. The  1[Provincial Government] may, by notification in the official Gazette,
exempt, conditionally or unconditionally, any undertaking or classes of undertakings from all or any
of the provisions of this Ordinance.
12. Saving. Nothing in this Ordinance applies to an undertaking which has not been in existence
at least for a period of two years, whether before or after the commencement of this Ordinance.
13. Powers to make rules.­(1) The 1[Provincial Government] may, subject to the condition of
previous publication, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Ordinance.
(2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may
provide for all or any of the following matters, namely:­
(a) the method and conditions of engagement and selection of apprentices and the period of
probation and appren ticeship;      
(b) the conditions and terms of a contract of apprentice ship;
(c) the method and procedure governing settlement of disputes between an apprentice and his
employer;
(d) the conditions of employment of apprentices after training;
(e) the working hours, leave and holidays for apprentices;
(f) the procedure of discipline, welfare, supervision and control of apprentices;
 (g) the forms of records to be maintained by the employers pertaining to the training of
apprentices;
(h) the periodical tests and grant of certificates on the successful conclusion of training;
(i) the standards for practical and related theoretical training;
(j) the composition, constitution and functions of, and the filling of vacancies in, the Tripartite
Advisory Committees, and the procedure to be followed by such Committee in the
discharge of their functions;
(k) any other matter which is to be or may be prescribed.
14. [Repeal.] Omitted by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Ordinance, 1981 (XXVII
of 1981), s. 3 and Sch., II.
